world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Betont werden die Worte immer auf der vorletzten Silbe, außer in einigen besonderen Fällen, wo die Betonung durch Akzente angegeben ist. Alle angehängten Partikeln und Pronomina gehen ganz im Worte auf, so daß sie auch den Akzent verlegen, z. B. tóta, aber totá-i.
new_statements.translation: Words are always stressed on the penultimate syllable, except in a few special cases, where the stress is indicated by accent marks. All attached particles and pronouns are fully absorbed into the word, so that they also shift the accent, e.g. tóta, but totá-i.
new_statements.citation: Tauern, Odo D. 1928. Beitrag zur Kenntnis der Sprachen und Dialekte von Seran. Anthropos 23(5-6): 1000-1020.
new_statements.locator: p. 1003, 'Kurzer Abriß einer Grammatik der Wemale-Sprache, wie sie in Japjo gesprochen wird', subsection 'Lautlehre' (last paragraph before 'Substantiva')
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (page scan, Anthropos 23, p. 1003, running head "Beitrag zur Kenntnis der Sprachen und Dialekte von Seran"). Under the bold heading "Kurzer Abriß einer Grammatik der Wemale-Sprache, wie sie in Japjo gesprochen wird" and subheading "Lautlehre", the last two sentences before the heading "Substantiva" read exactly: "Betont werden die Worte immer auf der vorletzten Silbe, außer in einigen besonderen Fällen, wo die Betonung durch Akzente angegeben ist. Alle angehängten Partikeln und Pronomina gehen ganz im Worte auf, so daß sie auch den Akzent verlegen, z. B. tóta, aber totá-i." Word-for-word identical to the reported quote (only typographic difference: "Betont" is letter-spaced for empha…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word; enclitic particles and pronominal/possessive suffixes count as part of the word, so stress moves right to stay penultimate (tóta -> totá-i). A few lexical exceptions carry written accents in Tauern's texts and vocabulary.
new_statements.exceptions: 'einige besondere Fälle' (a few special cases) with non-penultimate stress, marked by accents in the material; not enumerated.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word including attached particles and pronouns (stress re-computed on the whole cliticized form); based on Tauern's 1911-12 field notes on the dialect of Japjo (Yapio), a Wemale village of the Tala River basin (Collins 1983 calls the same notes 'on Ahiolo'), which lies in the former South Wemale [tlw] area rather than on the north coast.
new_statements.identity_note: sout2892 'South Wemale' [tlw] is a retired code: ISO 639-3 CR 2011-083 (held by the project) merged it into [weo] Wemale = Glottolog nort2864 in 2012 on the grounds that north and south Wemale are mutually intelligible dialects. The quoted statement is Tauern's sketch of Wemale 'as spoken in Japjo'; Collins 1983:54-56 treats those same notes as 'on Ahiolo' and groups Ahiolo with Hunitetu and Sanahu as Tala River basin villages, and Tala-area oral history calls the Ahiolo-Abio-Tala-Waraloin group 'Wemale Yapiopatai' (Japjo = Yapio). The Tala basin / Hunitetu-Waraloin-Kawe area is exactly what Ethnologue listed as South Wemale [tlw], so the statement describes the former South Wemale variety, not the north-coast (Horale/Kasieh/Uwenpantai) dialects. The catalog should file it once, under nort2864 (which already holds the same statement from the the compilation) with a dialect note 'Japjo/Ahiolo, Tala basin = former South Wemale [tlw]'; there is no separate current glottocode for the southern dialect. The modern South Wemale papers (Erniati & Sanjoko 2020, Hunitetu) are silent on stress.

sources.citation: Collins, James T. 1983. The historical relationships of the languages of Central Maluku, Indonesia. Pacific Linguistics D-47. Canberra: ANU. Section 4 'Perspectives on Wemale and Alune', pp. 52-56 and Map 6.
sources.note: Nothing on Wemale stress (historical sound changes only). Identity evidence: calls Tauern's sketch 'his notes on Ahiolo' (p. 54) and groups Hunitetu, Sanahu and Ahiolo as Tala River basin villages sharing *nd > d (p. 56); Map 6 places Ahiolo in the interior Tala basin near Waraloin and above Hunitetu.
Nothing; gives north dialects Horale, Kasieh, Uwenpantai and south dialects Waraloin, Honitetu, Kawe; ~5,000 north / ~3,700 south speakers.
